entry_point: The on-disk workspace operations behind the plan/apply API, pull-request events and DELETE /locks: FileWorkspace.Clone/GetWorkingDir/GetPullDir/Delete/DeleteForWorkspace/DeletePlan, the DefaultProjectCommandRunner Plan/Apply/PolicyCheck/Version/Import/StateRm execution paths, and DefaultDeleteLockCommand (lock state read back from storage). Confirmed offline at the pinned commit by driving those product entry points with attacker-shaped values and observing the foreign directory or file touched.

verified.entry_point: Reproduced on the pinned (injected) tree with the hidden security suite: 15/15 security tests fail there (foreign directory removed, foreign plan file removed, a command step executed outside the workspace, an outside artefact created) while all 10 functional tests pass. With the reference fix applied, 15/15 security and 10/10 functional pass. The project's own tests for the affected area (server/events/models, server/core/config/raw, TestPendingPlanFinder) pass on the pinned tree and with the fix.
sites: server/events/working_dir.go:817 repoPullDir (DataDir/repos/<repo>/<pull>) — no per-level bound at the pinned commit
server/events/working_dir.go:821 cloneDir (pull dir + workspace) — no bound; the only guard is validateCloneDir's data-root prefix, and it is used only by Clone/MergeAgain
server/events/working_dir.go:803 Delete / :810 DeleteForWorkspace — os.RemoveAll on the unchecked path
server/events/working_dir.go:849 DeletePlan — joins the stored project path and the workspace under the unchecked clone dir
server/events/project_command_runner.go:459,704,752,811,837,883 — the six runners join ctx.RepoRelDir to the workspace checkout and stat/execute there with no containment
server/events/delete_lock_command.go:39,63 — DeleteLock/DeleteLocksByPull feed stored lock.Project.Path and lock.Workspace to DeletePlan

server/core/config/raw/project.go:138-148 (atlantis.yaml workspace validation) and server/events/models/models.go:165-167 (repo identity '..') — published-fix input validation; the task does not require them directly, a sink-level fix satisfies the invariant
verified.routes: No pattern-B route: the advisory's own protection is missing uniformly at the pinned commit, so there is no unmodified upstream route that an already-applied check covers. All tested routes are published-fix sites or the two injected siblings below.
injected_siblings: server/core/runtime/plan_step_runner.go: the plan step runner keeps a raw plan-output snapshot under a directory named after the project (filepath.Join(path, ".atlantis", "plan-output", ctx.ProjectName)); the project name comes through the repository config schema, whose URL-safety check replaces separators before comparing and therefore accepts path fragments. Runs after the plan step.

server/events/project_artifacts.go (called from BuildProjectContext, server/events/project_command_context_builder.go): while a plan command's context is built, the stale plan for the project is removed at filepath.Join(repoDir, prjCfg.RepoRelDir, planFilename). Runs before the command runner's containment check and is not reached through the working-dir helpers.
verified.services: none; offline after build (Go module and build caches warmed in both images)
verified.project_tests_run: server/events/models (all), server/core/config/raw (all), server/events -run '^TestPendingPlanFinder' — pass on pinned+injected and on the oracle; pristine copies are restored at grading time.

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: a panic aborts the Go test binary instead of returning the client error the invariant requires, so this class can only make the security group fail and cannot score as a pass.
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: path confinement has no role, peer or direction dimension; the same resolved path is used for reads, deletes and step execution.
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: the protected values are literal path fragments, not parsed identities; there is no parser whose output could differ from the string used to build the path.
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: containment is purely path-based; no external authority can return nothing and make the guard fail open.

traps.lever: base flaw / published-fix site (report target): repository identity and workspace in the working-directory operations
traps.shape: repository identity that walks above the managed data root (Delete, GetPullDir) and a workspace that resolves into another pull request's directory or another workspace directory of the same repository (DeleteForWorkspace, GetWorkingDir)
traps.where: server/events/working_dir.go:794-835 (repoPullDir, cloneDir, Delete, DeleteForWorkspace, GetWorkingDir, GetPullDir)
traps.reason_to_dismiss: none for the reported operation; the lever is that a fix that only bounds the repository identity to the data root, or reuses validateCloneDir's prefix check, still leaves the per-pull bound and the workspace slot open

traps.lever: how-type: project-relative directory (RepoRelDir) in every command runner — a normaliser that preserves '..' and a route where the protection never existed
traps.shape: RepoRelDir supplied to the plan/apply API (the API path is not validated by the comment parser or the repo-config schema): plain upward traversal, the same traversal spelled after a real component, and a path that leaves the workspace but stays inside the pull request directory
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the project directory looks like repository configuration that is normalised when it is parsed (filepath.Clean('./'+dir) preserves a leading '..'), and the reported problem is about workspaces and repository identities, not project directories

traps.lever: how-type: plan deletion fed by state saved earlier (producer off the check's path)
traps.shape: the project path and workspace recorded in a saved lock resolve outside the workspace checkout when the lock is deleted; reaches the file system through the lock store, not through request validation
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the lock store is written by the server after it has already validated a project, so its values read as internal and trustworthy; a fix that validates request fields never sees this path

traps.lever: injected sibling (how-type): plan-output artefact directory named from the project name
traps.shape: a project name in repository configuration that passes the schema's URL-safety check (which replaces separators before comparing) but is a relative path fragment; the plan step runner creates a directory from it after the plan runs
traps.where: server/core/runtime/plan_step_runner.go writePlanOutputSnapshot (injected; the published fix never touches this file)
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the project name is validated by the repository-config schema as URL-safe, and the artefact lives next to the project's other generated files, so the value reads as already trusted and the write as ordinary

traps.lever: injected sibling (how-type, ordering): stale-plan removal during command-context preparation, before the runner's check
traps.shape: the project directory supplied to the plan API is joined to the workspace checkout to remove the previous plan; this happens while the command is built, before the runner that later validates the same value
traps.where: server/events/project_artifacts.go removeStalePlan (injected; called from BuildProjectContext and never touched by the published fix)
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the command runner rejects a traversing project directory, so the same value looks covered; the removal runs earlier, while the command is being prepared
